key_insight: The paper introduces a fidelity-like accuracy metric for quantum annealing that evaluates the annealing process itself, not just final optimization success.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware designers a quantitative target for annealer quality and a way to compare quantum annealers against classical thermal dynamics on an objective scale.
method: Define an annealing accuracy ε as a quantum-annealing analog of gate fidelity.
Benchmark ε on Rydberg atom systems using variational quantum Monte Carlo with a thermal-annealing-inspired ansatz.
Cross-check with Green function quantum Monte Carlo to reach higher precision limits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark accuracies of about ε≈10^-2 to 10^-3 with variational QMC up to 100 million atoms, and ε≈10^-4 with Green function QMC up to 100,000 atoms.
watch_item: The metric is benchmarked on specific Rydberg-atom models and simulated annealing variants, so practical transfer to other annealing hardware and problem classes may require careful recalibration.
paper_title: A fidelity metric for quantum annealing benchmarked by extreme scaling quantum Monte-Carlo simulations
